In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heat shock protein-based vaccines have been shown to induce antigen-specific CD8 + T cell responses, but it is still not clear whether these responses are sufficient to induce protective immunity against tumors or infectious diseases.
heat shock proteins are able to cross-prime CTLs and to activate the antigen-specific T cells in a cross-priming manner.
the heat shock proteins are very promising tools in the field of vaccination, especially in the field of cancer immunotherapy and vaccination against intracellular pathogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat shock proteins are very good vehicles for the cross-presentation of exogenous antigen and that the heat shock protein-based vaccines can induce effective CD8+ T-cell response.
heat shock proteins can serve as effective adjuvants for induction of CD8+ T-cell response to exogenized antigens.
heat shock protein-based vaccination is a promising approach in cancer therapy and in prevention of viral diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross-presentation of exogenous antigens is a complex process involving many cellular pathways.
the heat shock protein-based vaccines are effective in the induction of antigen specific CD8+ T lymphocyte response and that the cross-priming is the key mechanism of this induction.
the cross-presentation of antigenic peptides bound to heat shock proteins is a very effective strategy for inducing CTL response and may be used for the design of effective cancer and viral vaccines.
